subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported observation-only `message:sending` event to the internal HOOK.md surface, or keep pre-send policy exclusively on typed plugin hooks?
rationale: Current documentation deliberately separates coarse internal side effects from ordered typed message policy, so adding this new public event and its timing semantics requires an explicit owner decision before repairing the implementation.

options.title: Add an observational event
options.body: Support one canonical `message:sending` internal event after typed policy succeeds, with documented non-blocking semantics and a narrow legacy-key normalization path.

options.title: Keep typed hooks only
options.body: Close the internal-event direction and direct pre-send inspection, rewriting, and cancellation to the documented typed `message_sending` plugin hook.

recommendation.title: Add an observational event
recommendation.body: Support one canonical `message:sending` internal event after typed policy succeeds, with documented non-blocking semantics and a narrow legacy-key normalization path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their maintainer-owned exactly-once outbound-hook PR is the closest active definition of ordering and channel delivery semantics.
